This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth gave
a defiant speech today saying an attempt to impeach him undermines service members and is
service members and is being made over policy disagreements.
President Trump gave this department what it has not had in a generation,
a commander in chief with the courage to lead and the resolve to win. I stand behind
every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them and I would do it again tomorrow.
Yesterday, outgoing Kentucky Republican Congressman Thomas Massey launched an effort to impeach Hegseth
over his handling of the unpopular war against Iran and other actions. A procedural vote on
whether to move forward with the impeachment is expected later today. House Republicans have
selected Ohio Republican Jim Jordan as their new minority leader in next year's Congress.
NPR's Claudia Grisales reports. House Judiciary Committee chairman Jim Jordan beat the number
two House Republican Steve Scalise to win the minority leadership role. A source familiar with
closed-door discussions but not authorized to speak publicly told NPR Jordan won by a vote of 106
to 73. Jordan will step into the role after House Speaker Mike Johnson said he would leave
leadership after last week's devastating losses in the midterm elections. The former college
wrestling coach said he's "battle tested" and ready to fight Democrats while Scalise had argued
he would score conservative wins fueled by his broad experience in leadership.
Claudia Grisales, NPR News, the Capitol. Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders says he will not support
Chuck Schumer to be the leader of the incoming Democratic majority in the Senate. If this
campaign was about anything it was about change and the need for the Democratic party in my view
to move in a new and bold direction. Schumer says he's confident he will win but the party's left
flank has called for new leadership. Meanwhile Republicans re-elected South Dakotas John Thune
as Republican Senate leader after steep losses in the midterm elections. The AI company Anthropic
is going to sell shares to the public soon hoping to raise as much as $64 billion, NPR's John Ruich
reports. The maker of the popular Claude AI model says the IPO will offer 825 million shares at a
target price of $70 to $78 per share. With the company's existing shares that would put the value
of Anthropic as high as $1.4 trillion, just weeks ago analysts were saying the five-year-old
company's IPO valuation could be as high as $2 trillion. That would be the biggest ever beating
Elon Musk's SpaceX which was worth $1.75 trillion when it IPO'd in June. But investors have been
growing nervous about AI related companies which are spending heavily to develop AI without an
ironclad path to profitability. The IPO is expected next week. John Ruich, NPR News.
U.S. stocks fell today after reports showed inflation was worse than expected. This is NPR News.
A shareholder is suing Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang accusing them of deceiving investors about
Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy. The lawsuit claims the affair threatened national
security. President Trump said the FBI is investigating the matter. Huang has admitted
to and apologized for the affair. Concerns have arisen that Beijing may have orchestrated the
relationship to access Nvidia microchips that are crucial for AI development but restricted from
export to China. A handwritten copy of Martin Luther King Jr.'s "I Have a Dream" speech is
going up for auction early next year. NPR's Jason Derose reports it's a newly identified draft of the
iconic speech. Martin Luther King Jr. spoke on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial in 1963.
"Five score years ago, a great American in whose symbolic shadow we stand today."
Christie's in New York is auctioning off the seven yellow legal pad pages covered in blue cursive.
Some lines scratched out, others scribbled in the margins.
Researchers recently discovered the draft among the papers of one of King's advisors.
The auction house says a portion of the proceeds will go to the Martin Luther King Jr.
Center for Nonviolent Social Change. Jason Derose, NPR News.
The national average price for a gallon of regular gas has fallen below $4 a gallon for the first
time since July, $3.98. Some experts are predicting more price drops in the coming weeks in states
that suspended their gas taxes like Indiana, Ohio, Georgia and North Carolina could see even more.
I'm Rylan Barton. This is NPR News.
